# `filterdata`: keep points by return, class, or elevation {#sec-filterdata}

## What it does

`filterdata` writes a new point cloud holding only the points that pass a
filter: chosen return numbers, chosen classes, an elevation range, or any
combination. Typical uses are pulling out first returns for canopy
analysis, ground-classed points for checking a vendor's ground
classification, or points in an elevation band to inspect a suspected
artifact.

The return and class filters use the syntax shared by every tool
(@sec-point-filtering). The elevation limits `/minz` and `/maxz` apply to
raw elevation, not height above ground; to clip by height above ground,
use `clipdata` with `/ground` (@sec-clipdata).

## Example commands

The example runs three separate filters, each writing its own file. The
elevation band is a 20 ft window centered on the tile's median point
elevation.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/filterdata_commands.md >}}

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/output` | `out/filterdata/<name>.las` | The filtered point cloud. A `.laz` extension writes compressed output. |
| `/return` | `1` | Keep first returns only. `/return:first` does the same. |
| `/class` | `2` | Keep only points classified as ground (ASPRS class 2). |
| `/minz`, `/maxz` | `253`, `273` | Keep points with elevations from 253 to 273 ft. |

: Options used in the `filterdata` examples. {#tbl-options-filterdata}

## Outputs

One LAS or LAZ file per run, with the same point format, scale, offsets,
and coordinate system as the input. Withheld points and, unless `/class`
says otherwise, noise classes 7 and 18 are always left out.

## Results

@fig-filterdata-strip shows a west-east side view through the tile. Grey
points are the whole tile; blue points are what each filter kept.

- **First returns** mostly trace the top of the canopy, with some reaching
  the ground through gaps.
- **Ground class** points trace one thin line along the bottom of the
  point cloud, with nothing in the canopy.
- **Elevation band** points fill the space between the two dashed lines
  and nothing outside them.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/filterdata_figures.md >}}

## Checks

For each filter, the checks in @tbl-checks-filterdata confirm that the
number of points kept matches the same filter applied in R, that every
kept point satisfies the filter, that the coordinate system is kept, and
that withheld points are dropped.
